title: Finite fibre image of a proper algebraic-space family has finite closed image locally
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $p:X\to T$ and $q:Y\to T$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $h:X\to Y$ satisfy $qh=p$. Assume $p$ is proper and $q$ is separated and locally of finite type. These properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Let $t\in T$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of its residue field, and form the sheaf fibre products $X_{\bar t},Y_{\bar t}$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Suppose that the image of $|h_{\bar t}|:|X_{\bar t}|\to|Y_{\bar t}|$ is finite, where point spaces use [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Then there is an affine open neighbourhood $V\subseteq T$ of $t$, a closed subspace $j:Z\hookrightarrow Y_V$, and a $V$-morphism $a:X_V\to Z$ such that $h_V=ja$ and $Z\to V$ is finite. Here a closed subspace means that every scheme test is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]; finite means representable with every scheme base change finite in the sense of [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. In particular $Z$ is an affine scheme, with coordinate ring finite as a module over that of $V$. No flatness, reducedness, connectedness, or Noetherian hypothesis on $T$ is imposed; the finite image may be empty.

source.place: Tag 0AEJ, lemma-flat-proper-family-cannot-collapse-fibre, hypothesis (3)(a); shrink the resulting open base to an affine neighbourhood. Finite uses the representable convention of spaces-morphisms.tex definition-integral (Tag 03ZP).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-schematic-image] to the given $p,q,h$. It gives $h=iu$ through a closed subspace $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$, with $r:Z\to T$ proper and $|u|$ surjective. All hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses of the item.

The fibre-product point-image formula in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] applied to $u$ and $Z_{\bar t}\to Z$ makes $|u_{\bar t}|$ surjective. The point map of $i_{\bar t}$ is injective: equality of images means equality after a common field extension, and a closed immersion is a monomorphism, as its affine scheme tests are spectra of quotient rings [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Consequently $|i_{\bar t}|(|Z_{\bar t}|)=\operatorname{im}|h_{\bar t}|$ is finite, and hence $|Z_{\bar t}|$ is finite. This includes the empty image.

source.place: Tag 0AEJ, surjectivity on the field fibre and hypothesis (3)(a)

proof.text: Properness of $r$ implies separatedness and finite type by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-finite-fibre-quasifinite-criterion] to $r:Z\to T$ and $\Omega/\kappa(t)$. Its condition (i) holds by step 2, so $r$ is quasi-finite at every point over $t$.

By [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open] the quasi-finite locus $Q\subseteq|Z|$ is open. Set $C=|Z|\setminus Q$. Universal closedness of $r$ [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] makes $r(C)$ closed, and step 3 gives $t\notin r(C)$. Thus $W=T\setminus r(C)$ is an open neighbourhood of $t$. Choose an affine open $t\in V\subseteq W$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The inverse image of $V$ lies in $Q$; the base-change equality of quasi-finite loci in the first cited node shows that every point of $Z_V$ is quasi-finite over $V$.

source.place: Tag 0A4Y, lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood, proof; affine shrink by schemes.tex Tag 01IT

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change], $r_V:Z_V\to V$ is proper, hence separated. Its local quasi-finiteness is exactly quasi-finiteness at all points on every etale chart [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open, pqf-def-quasifinite]. Apply [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable] to represent $Z_V$ by a scheme over $V$. Taking its identity chart gives a locally quasi-finite scheme map; its properness agrees with scheme properness by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Therefore [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] makes $Z_V\to V$ finite.

source.place: Tag 0A4Y, final sentence, with spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0418 and scheme Tag 02LS (3) implies (1)

proof.text: Base-change $h=iu$ to $V$ to obtain the actual factorization $h_V=i_Vu_V$. The scheme tests of $i_V$ are scheme tests of $i$, so $i_V$ is a closed immersion. Finiteness of the scheme morphism $Z_V\to V$ persists on all scheme base changes by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], giving the required representable-finite convention. Since $V$ is affine, [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] says that $Z_V$ is affine with coordinate ring finite as a module over that of $V$. Rename $Z_V,i_V,u_V$ as $Z,j,a$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_closed_image_affine_neighbourhood (T : Scheme.{u}) (X Y : AlgebraicSpace T) (p : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (𝟙 T))) (q : Y ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (𝟙 T))) (h : X ⟶ Y) (w : h ≫ q = p) (hp : MapIsProper p) (hq : MapIsSeparated q) (hqlft : MapIsLocally (@LocallyOfFiniteType) q) (t : T) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra (T.residueField t) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (T.residueField t) Ω] (hfinite : (pointImage (finiteImageBaseChangeMap p q h w (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) Ω)) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t)) (V := Over.mk (𝟙 T)) (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (T.residueField t) Ω)) ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t)))).Finite) : ∃ (V : T.Opens), t ∈ V ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧ ∃ (Z : Over T) (g : Z ⟶ Over.mk V.ι) (j : yoneda.obj Z ⟶ Limits.pullback q.hom.hom (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk V.ι) (V := Over.mk (𝟙 T)) V.ι))) (a : Limits.pullback p.hom.hom (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk V.ι) (V := Over.mk (𝟙 T)) V.ι)) ⟶ yoneda.obj Z), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ f ↦ IsClosedImmersion f.left) j ∧ a ≫ j = finiteImageBaseChangeMap p q h w (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk V.ι) (V := Over.mk (𝟙 T)) V.ι) ∧ j ≫ pullback.snd q.hom.hom (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk V.ι) (V := Over.mk (𝟙 T)) V.ι)) = yoneda.map g ∧ a ≫ yoneda.map g = pullback.snd p.hom.hom (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk V.ι) (V := Over.mk (𝟙 T)) V.ι)) ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ f ↦ IsFinite f.left) (yoneda.map g) ∧ IsAffine Z.left ∧ (g.left.appTop).hom.Finite
